head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): strip wave-doc path annotations + retry-with-adaptation on wave-failed

Two defects caused v1.00.04 W3 to fail delivery verification despite
complete evidence, and left retries blind to the failure:

1. Wave-doc file-path annotations parsed into the path
   Wave docs annotate target files with explanatory prose in parens,
   e.g. "- File: q/docs/reports/test-regression-log.md (new:
   full-regression evidence log)". clean-file-path kept the parens in
   the parsed path, so gsd-wave-files held a path that never matches a
   real git file and delivery verification always reported "no wave
   target files changed". Now strips trailing " (...)" annotations
   (preserving real paths that contain parens without a leading space).

2. wave-failed retries had no adaptation context
   On delivery-verification failure the reason lived only in the
   campaign-result string; the follow-up run saw no reason and repeated
   the same mistake. try-complete-wave! now records the verifier message
   into the wave doc as a "## Last Failure" section (record-wave-failure!),
   and build-single-wave-prompt surfaces it as a "Previous Attempt
   Failed — Adapt" block so the next run addresses the failure.

Tests: +4 extract-last-failure unit tests, +5 clean-file-path / parser
annotation tests. GSD suite green (delivery-verifier 12, wave-completion
9, atomic-projection 7, campaign-state 24, go-orchestrator 39,
command-handlers-unit 31, plan-types).

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(gsd): delivery verifier must accept committed branch delivery

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): delivery verifier must accept committed branch delivery

Wave docs may instruct the wave agent to commit + push + open a PR
(e.g. v1.00.04 W0 impact-docs). The delivery verifier's
check-wave-files-changed only detected uncommitted working-tree
changes (git diff HEAD) and untracked files, so a wave that delivered
its work as commits on a feature branch failed verification with
'no wave target files changed' even though delivery evidence was
complete on GitHub.

Changed-files-set now also includes commits on the current branch
relative to its base (origin/main or main, three-dot diff), so both
delivery styles are recognized: uncommitted working-tree changes AND
committed feature-branch delivery.

Fixes the v1.00.04 W0 wave-failed (delivery verification) regression.

head_commit.message:
fix(test-impact): repair embed-impact-in-results! type bug causing silent-green CI failure

run-impact-selection! returns changed entries as plain path strings, but
embed-impact-in-results! unconditionally did (hash-ref c 'file), raising
a contract violation that the (with-handlers [exn:fail? (lambda (_) (void))])
swallowed — leaving impact-results.json WITHOUT its selection section.
The CI shadow guard (sel=0 AND esc=0 AND non_test>0) then correctly
failed the 'Step summary + shadow evidence record' step.

Fix (two parts):
- changed->path: accept both string entries (current) and hash entries
  with 'file (older callers), embedding changed_files as plain strings.
- Stop swallowing the handler silently: a failed evidence embed now
  prints the reason to stderr so it can never be a silent green again
  (W5 shadow-contract requirement).

Verified locally against the CI reproduction (merge-base b4ff6608 → head
20a5f27): selection now embeds with 23 escalations, escalated_broad=true,
68 changed_files — the guard condition is unsatisfiable.

head_commit.message:
ci(setup-racket): remove Xvfb startup from GitHub Actions

The 'Start Xvfb for TUI tests (Linux only)' step in the shared
setup-racket composite action hangs on GitHub-hosted runners
(apt-get/Xvfb launch is unreliable in the Actions sandbox),
blocking test shards and release-dry-run jobs from proceeding.

Removed the step entirely. The fast suite (used by all CI test
shards) excludes TUI files, and the TUI suite's only DISPLAY-
dependent test (tests/tui/test-clipboard.rkt) guards its X11
assertions behind (when (getenv "DISPLAY") ...) — so it passes
headlessly. No test or script depends on Xvfb.

head_commit.message:
fix(llm): wire per-model sse-read config into SSE stream timeouts

Previously the config key timeouts.models.<model>.sse-read was dead:
wire-timeouts! only read 'request', and the SSE stream timeouts came
from hardcoded constants (thinking cap held-request-detect-secs=120,
content http-stream-timeout-default=60). glm-5.3 (default provider,
no config entry) fell back to the 120s cap — the exact cause of the
repeated 'HTTP read timeout (120 seconds)' wave-cancelled failures.

Now:
- stream.rkt: new current-model-sse-read-timeouts parameter +
  effective-sse-read-timeout-for (returns #f when no override)
- mode-helpers.rkt: wire-timeouts! populates the new parameter from
  timeouts.models.<model>.sse-read
- openai-compatible.rkt: openai-stream-request threads the model's
  sse-read timeout through; the thinking/initial cap and the
  content-phase per-chunk timeout use it, falling back to the
  v0.99.78 defaults (120/60) when the model has no override

Effect: glm-5.3 (config sse-read=300) now tolerates 300s per-chunk
gaps in both phases; deepseek-v4-flash keeps its tight 60s window.
Config change: ~/.q/config.json timeouts.models.glm-5.3 = {request:900, sse-read:300}

(a) Default wave budget 3600s -> 7200s (policy.rkt). A live W3 wave
    performing area-by-area metadata migration + grouped-runner audit
    consumed the full 3600s while making steady progress and was killed
    mid-fix on a real runner defect (ZERO_PARSED/exit-guard).
(b) New current-gsd-wave-timeout-retries parameter (default 5, mirroring
    the campaign's LLM provider-retry ceiling): run-campaign-wave retries a
    timed-out run with a fresh session up to the ceiling; the attempt is
    NOT consumed by retries, only final exhaustion persists interrupted.
    (go-orchestrator.rkt)
(c) BUG-0017: TUI and GUI /go stop lines now include
    campaign-result-message alongside the status, so a wave-budget timeout
    is distinguishable from a cancellation/stale stop at a glance.
    (tui/commands.rkt, gui/slash-commands.rkt)

Tests: +4 go-orchestrator (retry ceiling, retry-then-success, retries=0
fail-closed), +1 TUI BUG-0017 message-rendering, policy default updated
(7200/5). All related suites pass; fast suite unchanged vs baseline.
README metrics re-synced.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(gsd): progress-aware consecutive-tool breaker + higher ceilings (BUG-0016)

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): progress-aware consecutive-tool breaker + higher ceilings (BUG-0016)

(a) Make the consecutive-tool circuit breaker progress-aware: a turn that
    edits a NEW distinct file resets the streak, so bulk metadata migrations
    touching hundreds of files are never mistaken for a runaway loop.
    (agent/iteration/loop-state.rkt edited-paths field, counters.rkt).
(b) Stamp toolLoopLimit onto the final loop-result metadata so the wave
    outcome distinguishes a deliberate breaker-stop ("tool loop limit
    reached") from a genuinely dropped tool result ("tool calls remain
    pending"). (runtime/iteration/step-executor.rkt)
(c) Raise ceilings: current-max-consecutive-tool-calls default 30 -> 300
    (util/iteration/decision.rkt); GSD campaign override 200 -> 600
    (extensions/gsd/policy.rkt; go-orchestrator inherits the policy value).

Tests: +6 (distinct/same-file/multi-file edit resets, breaker metadata
propagation); iteration/gsd suites all pass. README metrics re-synced.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(gsd): delivery verifier accepts issue-less campaigns + non-Racket waves

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): delivery verifier accepts issue-less campaigns + non-Racket waves

The /go delivery verifier falsely rejected two legitimate campaign shapes:

1. Issue-less campaigns (no per-wave GitHub issues) run on main/current
   branch, but check-branch-matches demanded feature/issue-N-wave derived
   from a STATE.md issue table. It now passes when no expected branch is
   derivable, and only honors STATE.md issue rows that reference the
   current plan's wave doc (stale rows from a previous campaign are
   ignored instead of being misread as issue mappings).

2. The compile gate ran 'raco make' on every changed wave file including
   ci.yml and .md docs, which fails on non-module files. It now filters to
   Racket sources only, and passes when no Racket targets changed
   (docs/CI-only wave) since the file-changed check already guarantees
   delivery evidence.

Root cause of the reported wave->coordinator->verification->next-wave
stall: W0's implementation+verification completed but the coordinator
marked the wave failed because the verifier rejected on both grounds.
Tests: +4 cases (issue-less main approval, stale STATE.md row ignored,
non-Racket compile gate). All 11 delivery-verifier tests + related GSD
suites pass.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(gsd): wave-doc authoring prompt warns against quarantined gh-wave-finish

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): wave-doc authoring prompt warns against quarantined gh-wave-finish

The github-integration extension already implements gh-wave-start,
gh-wave-finish, and gh-board as q tools; gh-wave-finish is deliberately
quarantined (fails closed by security policy) because the external
authenticated PR workflow is the sole finalization authority. The wave-doc
authoring prompt gave no guidance, so planning agents could write
gh-wave-finish Action steps that can never succeed agent-side (the cause of
the W6 wave-failed status). Adds explicit FINALIZATION guidance to the Wave
Doc Format section + regression test.

head_commit.message:
fix: iteration-budget default re-cap + edit-limit 500/1200 → 2000 (#9368)

Two latent issues surfaced by the user's live W3 re-test (2026-08-17 10:24+):
the iteration hard stop STILL fired at 80 and a whole-form edit was blocked
at 'old-text is too long (1376 chars, max 500)'.

1. tui-init make-campaign-runner: the wave budget defaulted to
   (dict-ref rt-config 'max-iterations 50) — when rt-config lacks the key,
   gsd-session-iteration-budget caps at 50 → resolve-max-iterations-hard
   re-caps at max(50*8/5, 80) = 80, silently defeating the v1.00.03 fix
   (current-gsd-wave-max-iterations 2000). Default now falls back to the
   policy value itself so the hard stop scales with the raised budget.

2. GSD edit-limit: the box default, reset-all-gsd-state!, and
   handle-plan-submit set 500; launch-wave-executor set 1200 — but the edit
   tool's SAFE-MAX-OLD-TEXT-LEN is 2000 and whole-form replacements routinely
   exceed 1200 (the user's 1376-char edit failed at 'max 500'). All GSD
   edit-limit sites now use 2000 so whole-form edits succeed up to the tool's
   documented max.

Tests updated: gsd-planning-edit-limit (default/raised 2000, accepts ≤2000,
rejects >2000), gsd-planning-state (default 2000), gsd-context-factory
(default 2000), gsd-planning-integration (/go → 2000), edit-balance-guard
(default 2000). Smoke (308) + extensions (1511) green.

head_commit.message:
fix: edit-tool leading-whitespace auto-fallback + D3 consecutive-tool ceiling 100→200 (#9366)

Root cause of the 2026-08-17 live W3 wave-failed (session
01M07A6YCFN12E8E0FYJFHT9FT): the executor edited a test file with old-text
whose leading whitespace was systematically +1 space per level (9/11/19 vs
the file's 8/10/18). The edit tool did exact whitespace matching, so all 6
edit attempts failed 'old-text not found'; the model kept recovering with
more tool calls (read/grep/edit) and the D3 consecutive-tool breaker fired at
100 after ~19 min / 101 iterations -> wave-failed.

Fixes:
1. edit-normalize: new strip-leading? option + leading-whitespace-normalization
   options; leading-ws-find-matches tolerates ONLY leading-whitespace drift
   (threshold 1.0 = byte-exact content after indent strip), returns unique
   spans, and expands the span back over whitespace to line start.
2. edit-contract: apply-edit-contract now auto-falls-back to the leading-ws
   match when exact fails (unique -> apply, multiple -> ambiguous, none ->
   not-found/fuzzy), so indentation-drift edits succeed instead of failing.
3. edit.rkt: success result surfaces 'Note: old-text matched after ignoring
   leading whitespace (indentation).' when the auto-fallback fired.
4. policy.rkt: current-gsd-max-consecutive-tool-calls 100 -> 200 so recovery

head_commit.message:
fix: edit-tool leading-whitespace auto-fallback + D3 consecutive-tool ceiling 100→200 (#9366)

Root cause of the 2026-08-17 live W3 wave-failed (session
01M07A6YCFN12E8E0FYJFHT9FT): the executor edited a test file with old-text
whose leading whitespace was systematically +1 space per level (9/11/19 vs
the file's 8/10/18). The edit tool did exact whitespace matching, so all 6
edit attempts failed 'old-text not found'; the model kept recovering with
more tool calls (read/grep/edit) and the D3 consecutive-tool breaker fired at
100 after ~19 min / 101 iterations -> wave-failed.

Fixes:
1. edit-normalize: new strip-leading? option + leading-whitespace-normalization
   options; leading-ws-find-matches tolerates ONLY leading-whitespace drift
   (threshold 1.0 = byte-exact content after indent strip), returns unique
   spans, and expands the span back over whitespace to line start.
2. edit-contract: apply-edit-contract now auto-falls-back to the leading-ws
   match when exact fails (unique -> apply, multiple -> ambiguous, none ->
   not-found/fuzzy), so indentation-drift edits succeed instead of failing.
3. edit.rkt: success result surfaces 'Note: old-text matched after ignoring
   leading whitespace (indentation).' when the auto-fallback fired.
4. policy.rkt: current-gsd-max-consecutive-tool-calls 100 -> 200 so recovery
   loops that re-read/re-grep before retrying are not policy-killed.

Tests: edit-normalize (strip-leading normalization, coordinate mapping),
edit-matching-correctness (auto-fallback applies when unique / ambiguous /
not-found on content diff), edit-execution-parity (ws fallback succeeds with
Note, genuine content mismatch still fails with diagnostics), gsd-policy
(ceiling >= 200 <= 400). Smoke (308) + extensions (1511) suites green.

head_commit.message:
fix: /go wave UX — remove iteration hard-stop, restore thinking display, show tool file paths (#9364)

User findings from a live /go session:

1. Wave cancelled at iteration 80: current-gsd-wave-max-iterations was 50,
   so the derived hard limit was only 80. Raised the wave budget to 2000 so
   the hard ceiling scales to 3200+; waves are bounded by the 1800s timeout
   and the 100-consecutive-tool breaker, not an 80-iteration kill.

2. Thinking not displayed: handle-session-started/resumed read payload
   'sessionId but real session.started events carry the sid in the ENVELOPE
   (event-session-id) and payload key 'session-id. The handler returned "",
   resetting ui-state-session-id to empty, which dropped every
   model.stream.thinking delta via event-can-activate-stream?. Fall back to
   event-session-id and the hyphen payload key.

3. [TOOL] read/edit showed no filename: extract-arg-summary fell through to
   the first-value branch, showing 'read: 156' (line limit) and
   'edit: <old-text>'. Prefer path/file keys in the TUI arg summary.

Tests: SE4 thinking-after-real-session.started (5/5), read/edit path display
(27/27), wave budget floor (policy suite green).

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): S2b/D5 — executor working-directory contract + file-target validation (#9359)

Campaign 81f9be4b: attempt-3 burned tool budget on repo-root vs q/ cwd
confusion ('Wrong working dir', 'raco make says file not found');
attempt-5 read q/tui/key-dispatch.rkt when the plan declares
q/tui/keybindings/key-dispatch.rkt (dropped path segment).

Fix (build-single-wave-prompt):
- Inject a '## Working Directory Contract' block into every single-wave
  prompt: project root (base-dir), process working directory, and the
  explicit rule that File: paths resolve relative to the project root
  (source lives in the 'q' subdir).
- Validate every declared File: target against base-dir up front and
  annotate [exists] / [MISSING] so the executor can distinguish a
  genuinely absent file from a path-resolution mistake instead of
  burning iteration budget rediscovering it.

Tests: tests/test-gsd-d5-executor-cwd-contract.rkt (4) — contract block
present with root/cwd/rule, exists annotation, MISSING annotation, and
full target enumeration in order.

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): S2a — truncate lease lock before rewrite + sanitize empty owner (#9358)

Campaign 81f9be4b attempt-5 lock corruption: open-output-file 'can-update
does NOT truncate, so file-position 0 + write left a stale tail from the
previous (longer) owner — observed: . The lease file became
unreadable, defeating D4 owner diagnostics. The re-dispatch path also
wrote (owner . ""), so a stale lease could not be attributed.

Fix:
- file-truncate port 0 before rewriting the lease.
- Sanitize owner: empty/missing session-id falls back to "unknown".
- campaign-lease records the sanitized owner.

Tests: test-gsd-go-orchestrator.rkt +2 — stale-tail truncation regression
(previous longer owner must not leave fragments) and empty-owner
sanitization.
